text: Welcome to our guessing game! Before you begin your task, you'll complete a brief guided tutorial (~2 minutes) to understand the game.

You're watching someone play the treasure game. The player controls a character and their goal is to collect one of the four gems (triangle, square, hexagon, or circle). The rules of the game are as follows: The player can move on the white squares. The player has a full view of the map at all time. The player's goal is to collect exactly one target gem.

Keys unlock doors of the same color (e.g. red keys unlock red doors). Each key can only be used once. Keys disappear after use. Each box may be empty or contain exactly one key. The player may or may not know what's in each box. Neither you nor the player can see what's hidden in each box. But both of you can see all other objects in the scene. There are at most two keys hidden among the boxes. The player knows that the puzzle is solvable, which means there are just enough keys to reach any of the target gems.
Your task is to figure out what the player's goal is, and also what the player believes about the contents of the boxes.

At each step in this game, you will watch the player take several actions. We will then ask you one question about the player's goal, and another set of questions about what the player initially believed at the start of the game.

queries.prompt: How many gems is the player trying to collect?

queries.prompt: Which of the following is true?
option: The player has no knowledge about the contents of each box.
The player knows perfectly what's inside each box.
The player might know exactly what's in each box, but might also be unsure.

queries.prompt: You see the player walk towards box 1 and open it, finding that it is empty. The player then walks to box 2 and picks up the red key they find inside. Which statement is the most plausible?
option: The player initially thought there was a red key in box 1.
The player initially knew there was a red key in box 1.
The player initially thought there was a red key in box 2.

queries.prompt: You're watching the player and two of the gems seem likely to be the player's goal, but you're not sure which. What should you do?
option: Guess one of the two likely gems, and hope for the best.
Guess both likely gems, because you're not sure.
Guess all of the gems, because who knows?
